caption: Figure 9. (a) Tensor parallelism: each transformer block is assigned to multiple CXL devices. Prompts are processed se- quentially. (b) In a transformer block, fully connected layers are spread across CXL devices, while other operations are confined to a single device.

templates.why_chosen: Two lettered panels with one shared legend placed below and spanning both.
templates.what_to_learn: When both panels use the same colour encoding, the legend goes below spanning the full width - never duplicated per panel.

templates.why_chosen: A minor but real phase device: panel (a) runs one vertical time arrow past stacked Decoder 0/1/2 boxes showing a prompt's blocks processed one at a time, before panel (b) zooms into the per-layer mapping.
templates.what_to_learn: When only one stage of a bigger figure is genuinely sequential, don't force the whole thing into lanes: draw one small vertical time arrow beside the sequential boxes (Decoder 0, 1, 2...) and keep the rest of the figure as an ordinary architecture diagram.

templates.why_chosen: Panel (a)'s coarse per-decoder timeline sits beside panel (b)'s detailed per-layer device map, sharing one blue-single-device/green-multi-device legend so the reader sees which decoder runs when and which of its layers pay the broadcast/gather cost.
templates.what_to_learn: Pair a coarse timeline/mapping overview with one detailed per-layer zoom, and carry a single two-colour legend (single-device vs multi-device placement) across both panels so the coarse view and the fine view never need separate keys.
